definitions.title: The Power Rule for Differentiation
definitions.statement: For any real number n, the derivative of x^n with respect to x is n*x^(n-1).
conditions: x > 0 if n is not an integer
Domain exclusions at x = 0 if n < 1
definitions.explanation: One of the most widely used rules in calculus, valid for positive integers, negatives, fractions, and irrational exponents.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Multiply by the exponent, then decrement the exponent by 1.

definitions.title: The Product Rule
definitions.statement: The derivative of a product of two differentiable functions is the derivative of the first times the second, plus the first times the derivative of the second.
conditions: Both u and v must be differentiable at x
definitions.explanation: Derived geometrically from the expansion of a rectangle's area: Delta(uv) = u*Delta(v) + v*Delta(u) + Delta(u)*Delta(v).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Derivative of a product is NOT the product of derivatives: (uv)' = u'v + uv'.

definitions.title: The Quotient Rule
definitions.statement: The derivative of a quotient of two differentiable functions is low d-high minus high d-low over the square of what's below.
conditions: Both u and v differentiable at x
definitions.explanation: Notice the minus sign in the numerator; the order of differentiation is critical.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Quotient rule numerator has subtraction: (u/v)' = (u'v - uv') / v^2.
